newsitem.title: MEXICO: MEXICO STOCKS UP ON LIGHT BARGAIN-HUNTING.
newsitem.headline: MEXICO STOCKS UP ON LIGHT BARGAIN-HUNTING.

text.p: Mexican stocks opened up on Tuesday due to what traders said was mild bargain-hunting carried over from the prior session driven by less pressure on the U.S. long bond.
"The market slid in thin volume yesterday and then we saw some buying on dips, and basically we are seeing some of that following through," a desk trader said.
The leading IPC share index was up 26.02 points in the early minutes of trade, or 0.52 percent, at 5,069.67. Volume was thin at 2.1 million shares traded.
"The market is still on hold while awaiting the impact of U.S. inflation data on Thursday, but the long bond helps," a floor trader said.
The 30-year Treasury bond was up 14/32 to yield 6.61 percent in early trade.
Dealers said market heavyweight Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex), which accounted for half of all shares traded in early dealing, was pulling up the market.
Telmex was up 35 centavos to 20.90 pesos, while its ADRs had decoupled from the Dow Jones and were up 5/16 to 53-3/8.
The Dow Jones was meanwhile off 0.46 point to 8,061.65.
Financial group Bancomer A shares had also recovered at relatively brisk trade, and were ahead 8 centavos to 3.58 pesos.
On the broad market, gainers far outpaced decliners by 18 to two, out of 28 stocks that had changed hands.
